Rashi on Nedarim 14a:1:1.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Yehuda - Who holds [that] from a negative [statement, you infer] a positive [statement].

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:1:2.hebrew: היינו רישא - כלומר, כבר תנינא בפירקין דלעיל (נדרים דף י:): לחולין שאוכל לך, לא כשר וכו', ומוקמינן לה כרבי יהודה. ומאי קא משמע לן הכא? אלא ודאי לא איצטריך הכא חולין, אלא איידי דבעא למיתני כבשר חזיר, כעבודת כוכבים, תנא נמי חולין:
Rashi on Nedarim 14a:1:2.english: This is [identical to] the first clause - That is to say, we already learned in the previous chapter (Nedarim 10b): "[That which] I eat of yours [shall be] like non-sacred food," "[that which I eat of yours shall be] not kosher," etc., and we establish it in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda; so what does [the Tanna] teach us here? Rather, it is certain that [the case of] non-sacred food was not necessary here; rather, because he wanted to teach "like pig meat, like idolatrous worship," he taught "non-sacred food" as well.

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:3:1.hebrew: רבינא אומר - הא דקתני חולין, לאו דאמר חולין שאוכל, אלא הכי קתני: אלו מותרין כחולין, האומר כבשר חזיר, כעבודת כוכבים כו':
Rashi on Nedarim 14a:3:1.english: Ravina says - That which [the Mishnah] taught "non-sacred [food]" is not that he said, "Non-sacred [food] that I will eat"; rather, this is what it teaches: "These are permitted like non-sacred [food]: one who says 'like pig meat,' 'like idol worship,' etc."

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:3:2.hebrew: ואי לא תנא חולין - דמשמע מותר כחולין הוא, הוה אמינא בעי שאלה לחכם — היכא דאמר כבשר חזיר או כעבודת כוכבים, בעי למישאל אי הוה נדר אי לא. ולהכי תנא חולין, למימר דחולין גמורין נינהו, דלא בעי שאלה:
Rashi on Nedarim 14a:3:2.english: And if it did not teach non-sacred [food] - which implies [that] it is permitted like non-sacred [food], I would have said [that] it requires a request to a Sage: where one said "like pig meat" or "like idol worship," he must ask whether it is a vow or not. And therefore it taught "non-sacred [food]" to say that they are completely non-sacred, [so] that it does not require a request [to a Sage].

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:4:1.hebrew: ומי איכא לאסוקי אדעתא - דבעי שאלה היכא דנדר כהאי גוונא, אי לא תני נמי חולין:
Rashi on Nedarim 14a:4:1.english: And could one consider - that it requires a request [for dissolution] where he vowed in such a manner, if it had not also taught [the case of] non-sacred [food]?

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:4:2.hebrew: והא מדקתני סיפא האומר לאשתו הרי את אסורה כאימא - אע"ג דנדר בדבר האסור, דלא הוי נדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 14a:4:2.english: And [from] that which the latter clause teaches: One who says to his wife, "Behold, you are forbidden like [my] mother" - Even though he vowed by a forbidden thing, which is not a [valid] vow [nevertheless, it requires dissolution].

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:4:3.hebrew: פותחין לו פתח ממקום אחר - לנודר זה לחרטה, שצריך לבא לפני חכם, ואין פותחין לו לומר: הואיל ונדרת בדבר האסור, לא כלום נדרת, אלא מפתח אחר מראין לו ההיתר, כדי שלא יקל את ראשו לכך. כלומר, להכי מצרכינן ליה שאלה ופותחין לו פתח ממקום אחר, כדי שלא יהא קל בעיניו לידור בכך, להזכיר אמו לגנאי. ומדקתני בהא סיפא דצריך שאלה, מכלל דרישא דלא קתני לא צריך שאלה, ואפילו אי לא אמר חולין לא מצרכינן ליה שאלה:
Rashi on Nedarim 14a:4:3.english: They broach with him an opening from another place - For this vower, for regret, as he must come before a Sage; and they do not broach [dissolution] with him by saying, "Since you vowed by a forbidden thing, you have vowed nothing," rather, they show him the release from another opening, so that he will not treat this lightly. That is to say, for this reason we require him [to make] a request [to a Sage] and broach with him an opening from another place: so that it will not be light in his eyes to vow in this manner, to mention his mother in a derogatory way. And from [the fact] that it teaches in this latter clause that it requires a request [to a Sage], it follows by inference that the first clause, where it does not teach [this], does not require a request [to a Sage], and even if he did not say "non-sacred," we do not require him [to make] a request [to a Sage].

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:4:4.english: Rather, non-sacred [food] was cited incidentally - It cited it needlessly.

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:6:1.english: For it is also written: “to bind a bond [issar]” - And let us also say: until one vows by a forbidden [asur] item.

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:7:1.english: He has said nothing - Thus, he does not even require a request [for dissolution].

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:8:1.hebrew: לא אמר כלום מדאורייתא - הואיל דנדר בדבר האסור, ומ"מ צריך שאלה כדי שלא יקל את ראשו בכך:
Rashi on Nedarim 14a:8:1.english: He has said nothing by Torah law - Since he vowed regarding a forbidden matter; nevertheless, he needs a request [for absolution] so that he does not treat it lightly.

Rashi on Nedarim 14a:8:2.hebrew: תלמיד חכם - לא בעי שאלה, דאקרי בעלמא היא דאירע לו, ולא יקל את ראשו בכך. ומתני' מיירי בעם הארץ, דאי אמרת אפילו שאלה לא בעי, יקל את ראשו להיות נודר כך:
Rashi on Nedarim 14a:8:2.english: A Torah scholar - [He] does not require a request [for annulment], for it was a mere happenstance that occurred to him, and he will not act lightly because of this. And the Mishnah speaks of an ignoramus, for if you say he does not even require a request [for annulment], he will act lightly to vow in this manner.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:1:1.hebrew: היינו רישא - פירוש: מתני' דפ"ק, דתנא: "לחולין שאוכל לך, לא כשר" וכו', ואוקימנא כרבי יהודה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:1:1.english: This is the first clause - Explanation: [this refers to] the Mishnah of the first chapter, where it teaches: "[That which] I eat of yours [shall be] as non-sacred; not kosher," etc., and we established it as [following] Rabbi Yehuda.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:2:1.hebrew: איידי דתנן כבשר חזיר - וכייל דברים הרבה שאין הנדר חל, תנא נמי "חולין" בהדייהו; דבעי ליישב לעולם מתני' לאוקמה דאיצטריך למידק "הא לחולין", וכר' יהודה, ואע"ג דתנינא חדא זימנא פ"ק, תנייה אגב גררא. ול"נ דלאו לדוקיא אתיא מתני', אלא לגופיה; אע"ג דלא הוי שום רבותא, מ"מ תנינא אגב גררא דאינך, והשתא מתוקמא גם כר"מ, ולהכי לא הוי מצי למיתני "קרבן שאוכל לך":
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:2:1.english: Since we learned "like pig's meat" - and [the Mishnah] groups together many things regarding which a vow does not take effect, it also taught "non-sacred" along with them; for [the Gemara] still wishes to reconcile the Mishnah by establishing it as needing [to teach "non-sacred"] in order to infer "but [if he says] le-chullin, [it is forbidden]," in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, and even though we already taught it once in the first chapter, it taught it [here] incidentally. But it appears to me that the Mishnah does not come for an inference, rather for itself; even though there is no novelty [in it], nevertheless we taught it incidentally to those other [cases], and now it is established even according to Rabbi Meir, and for this reason it could not have taught "an offering that I eat from you."

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:3:1.hebrew: ה"א דבעי שאלה מדרבנן, ומי מצי למימר הכי, והא מדקתני סיפא - וא"ת: היכא ס"ד דבעי שאלה מדרבנן, והא קתני דמותרין? וי"ל: דס"ד דמותרין ר"ל מדאורייתא; וכה"ג אמרינן לקמן: "ד' נדרים התירו חכמים", ואפ"ה קאמר בגמרא דבעי שאלה מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:3:1.english: "I would say that it requires a request [for dissolution] by rabbinic law. And can one say this? Behold, since the latter clause teaches..." - And if you ask: How could it enter your mind that it requires a request [for dissolution] by rabbinic law, when [the Mishnah] teaches that they are permitted? One can answer: [The Gemara] initially thought that "permitted" means by Torah law; and similarly we say later [in the tractate]: "Four vows the Sages permitted," and even so the Gemara says that it requires a request [for dissolution] by rabbinic law.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:4:1.hebrew: ה"א דבעי שאלה מדרבנן, ומי מצי למימר הכי, והא מדקתני סיפא - וא"ת: היכא ס"ד דבעי שאלה מדרבנן, והא קתני דמותרין? וי"ל: דס"ד ד"מותרין" ר"ל מדאורייתא, וכה"ג אמרינן לקמן: "ד' נדרים התירו חכמים", ואפ"ה קאמר בגמרא דבעי שאלה מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:4:1.english: "One might have thought that it requires rabbinic inquiry [for dissolution], and how could one say this, since the latter clause teaches..." - And if you ask: How could it have entered your mind that it requires rabbinic inquiry, when [the Mishnah] teaches that they are permitted? One can say that it entered your mind that "they are permitted" means [permitted] by Torah law; and similarly we say later: "The Sages permitted four vows," and even so the Gemara says that they require rabbinic inquiry.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:6:1.hebrew: אי הכי אפי' בדבר האסור נמי דהא כתיב לאסור איסר - וא"ת, א"כ, "כי ידור נדר" לדבר הנדור למה לי? וי"ל: דלא תימא דדבר האסור חמיר (פי') [טפי] להתפיס בו מדבר הנדור:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:6:1.english: If so, even [with] a forbidden item as well, for it is written: "To bind [his soul with] a bond [issar]" - And if you say: If so, why do I need [the phrase] "When a man vows a vow" [to teach that a vow takes effect when associated] with a vowed item? And one can say: [It is needed] so that you should not say that a forbidden item is more stringent to associate [a vow] with than a vowed item.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:6:2.hebrew: ההיא מיבעי' ליה לכדתניא איזהו איסר האמור בתורה וכו' - דמוקי לה בשבועות פ"ג (דף כ.) למתפיס בנדר או למתפיס בשבועה, שאומ' "זה כזה", ונפקא לן מכפילות הלשון ד"לאסור איסר". וא"ת: התינח לאביי, דמוקי ליה הכי פ"ג דשבועות; אלא לרבא, דאמר התם מתפיס בשבועה ובנדר לא כלום הוא, והך ברייתא מפרש לה: "ואיזה הוא איסר נדר האמור בתורה? הרי שאמר: הרי עלי שלא לאכול בשר וכו'", דכיון שמזכיר בהדיא שלא לאכול, הוי עיקר הנדר, ומסברא נפקא ליה ולא משום פסוק — א"כ לדידיה כפילות ד"לאסור איסר" למה לי? ושמא יש לומר, דלרבא אין להקשות מן הכפילות מ"לאסור איסר", משום דרבא אמר התם דאיסר הוא לשון בפני עצמו: [ואם] הוציאו בלשון נדר — נדר, כגון שאמר "ככר זה עלי לאיסור"; ואם הוציאו בלשון שבועה, שאמר "איסור שלא יאכל (בדבר) [ככר] זה" — הוי כאילו אמר "שבועה שלא אוכל ככר זה". ודריש ליה התם משום דאיסר זה הטילו הכפילות בין נדר לשבועה. וכיון דלשון הוא לעצמו, ליכא למידרש מן הכפילות שיתפיס בדבר, מידי דהוה אשבועה, דכתיב "או השבע שבועה" — כפילות, ואפילו הכי לא דרשינן מן הכפילות שיתפיס בדבר האסור ע"י שבועה בכפילות מנדר, משום דגלי קרא בעלמא "לא תשבעו בשמי לשקר", דמשמע שהוא לשון לעצמו, שאסר עצמו בלשון שבועה. הילכך לרבא לא קשיא כלל מן הכפילות, כדפרי'. כך נראה למורי שי':
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:6:2.english: "That [phrase] is necessary for that which is taught [in a baraita]: What is the bond [issar] mentioned in the Torah, etc." - For [the Gemara] establishes it in Shevuot, Chapter 3 (20a), as referring to one who associates [an item] with a vow or one who associates [an item] with an oath, who says "this is like that," and we derive it from the doubling of the wording "to bind with a bond" [le'esor issar]. And if you ask: This works well according to Abaye, who establishes it thus in the third chapter of Shevuot; however, according to Rava — who says there that one who associates [an item] with an oath or with a vow, it is nothing, and he explains this baraita [as]: "And what is the issar of a vow mentioned in the Torah? Behold, one who says: 'It is [incumbent] upon me not to eat meat,' etc.," for since he explicitly mentions "not to eat," it is the essence of the vow, and it is derived from logic and not from a verse — if so, according to him, why do I need the doubling of "to bind with a bond"? And perhaps one can say that according to Rava, one should not raise a difficulty from the doubling of "to bind with a bond," because Rava says there that issar is an independent expression: [if] he uttered it in the language of a vow, [it is] a vow — such as when he said, "This loaf is upon me as an issar"; and if he uttered it in the language of an oath, where he said, "An issar that he will not eat this (thing) [loaf]," it is as though he said, "An oath that I will not eat this loaf." And he expounds it there because this issar — the doubling placed it between a vow and an oath. And since it is an independent expression, one cannot expound from the doubling that he can associate [an item] with something [else], just as it is with an oath, where it is written "or swear an oath" — a doubling — and even so we do not expound from the doubling that he can associate [an item] with a forbidden thing by means of an oath through the doubling [any more] than [by means of] a vow, because a verse elsewhere reveals, "You shall not swear by My name falsely," which implies that it is an independent expression, where he forbade himself with the language of an oath. Therefore, according to Rava, there is no difficulty at all from the doubling, as I have explained. So it appears to my teacher, may he live.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:7:1.hebrew: ורמינהו הרי את עלי וכו' - יודע היה דמתניתין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:7:1.english: And they raised a contradiction: "You are hereby to me," etc. - He knew that [the ruling of] the Mishnah:

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:7:2.hebrew: ורמינהו הרי את עלי וכו' - יודע היה דמתניתין דבעי התרת חכם אינו כ"א מדרבנן, דדבר הנדור בעי; אלא ס"ד דהך ברייתא דקתני "לא אמר כלום", אפי' מדרבנן לא בעי שאלה, מדקתני "לא אמר כלום". וכן מוכח שינויא דאביי, דקאמר: לא אמר כלום מדאורייתא וצריך שאלה מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:7:2.english: And [the Gemara] raises a contradiction: "You are hereby to me," etc. - [The questioner] knew that [the ruling of] our Mishnah, that he requires dissolution by a sage, is only by rabbinic law, since [biblically] it requires [comparison to] a vowed item; rather, it entered [the questioner's] mind that this baraita, which teaches "he has said nothing," [means] he does not even require a request [for dissolution] by rabbinic law, since it teaches "he has said nothing." And so [too] is proven by Abaye's answer, who says: He has said nothing by Torah law, and he requires a request [for dissolution] by rabbinic law.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:7:3.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> בהך ברייתא: "הרי את עלי כבשר אמי כבשר אחותי", ואאחותו של הבעל קאי. אבל <abbr title="לא גרסינן">ל"ג</abbr> "כבשר אמה כבשר אחותה", דמשמע דאמה ואחותה של אשתו קאי. <abbr title="ולא נהירא">ול"נ</abbr>, <abbr title="דאם כן">דא"כ</abbr> הוה ליה למימר "כבשר אמך או כבשר אחותך", דהא במדבר עם אשתו מיירי, כדקאמר "הרי את עלי". אלא <abbr title="גרסינן">גר'</abbr> "כבשר אמי כבשר אחותי", אך הסופרים טעו לכתוב "אמה ואחותה":
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:7:3.english: This is how we read in this baraita: "You are hereby to me like the flesh of my mother, like the flesh of my sister," and it refers to the husband's sister. However, we do not read "like the flesh of her mother, like the flesh of her sister," which implies that it refers to his wife's mother and sister. And [that reading] does not seem [correct], for if so, it should have said "like the flesh of your mother or like the flesh of your sister," since it is dealing with [a husband] speaking with his wife, as it says, "You are hereby to me." Rather, we read "like the flesh of my mother, like the flesh of my sister," but the scribes erred in writing "her mother and her sister."

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:8:1.hebrew: רבא אמר הא בתלמיד חכם הא בעם הארץ - ואביי, מדלא משני הכי, משמע לדידיה דאין חילוק בין תלמיד חכם לעם הארץ, ואפי' בת"ח בעי שאלה מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:8:1.english: Rava said: This [refers] to a Torah scholar, [and] that [refers] to an ignoramus - And [as for] Abaye, since he does not answer thus, it implies that according to him there is no distinction between a Torah scholar and an ignoramus, and even in [the case of] a Torah scholar, he requires a request [for absolution] by rabbinic law.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:9:1.hebrew: והתניא הנודר בתורה וכו' - פירוש: "והתניא" בניחותא, שיש חילוק בין ת"ח לעם הארץ:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14a:9:1.english: And it is taught [in a baraita]: One who vows by a Torah [scroll], etc. - Explanation: "And it is taught" is [to be read] as a statement [and not as a question], [indicating] that there is a distinction between a Torah scholar and an ignoramus.
